must_remember: Refractive index ($mu$) of lens material varies inversely with wavelength ($lambda$) according to Cauchy's relation: $mu = A + \frac{B}{lambda^2}$.
Violet light ($lambda$ is short) has a higher refractive index than red light ($lambda$ is long), so $mu_v > mu_r$.
Longitudinal Chromatic Aberration (LCA) for a single thin lens is given by $LCA = f_r - f_v = omega f_y$.
Dispersive power ($omega$) is given by $omega = \frac{mu_v - mu_r}{mu_y - 1} = \frac{f_r - f_v}{f_y}$.
The condition for achromatism of two thin lenses in contact is $\frac{omega_1}{f_1} + \frac{omega_2}{f_2} = 0$.
For two lenses of the same material separated by a distance $d$, the condition for achromatism is $d = \frac{f_1 + f_2}{2}$.

glossary.meaning: Failure of a lens to focus all colors to the same point due to wavelength-dependent refractive index.
Ratio of the difference in focal lengths for extreme colors to the focal length for the mean color.
Axial separation between the focal points of extreme colors (violet and red).
Difference in image sizes for different wavelengths formed perpendicular to the optical axis.
Combination of two lenses designed to bring at least two extreme wavelengths to a common focus.
